title: Reach into a record that may be missing

blocks.md:
## `?.` asks first

`signal.beacon.name` throws the moment `signal.beacon` is `undefined`. `signal?.beacon?.name` stops at the first missing link and hands back `undefined` instead of throwing.

`?.` does **not** supply a default. It only avoids the crash. Pair it with `??` when you want a fallback:

```
signal?.beacon?.name ?? "unknown"
```

There are two more forms: `fn?.()` calls only if `fn` exists, and `list?.[0]` indexes only if `list` exists.

blocks.promptMd: A beacon reads `{ name: "", power: 0 }`. Which expression keeps both real readings instead of hiding them?
blocks.explainMd: `""` and `0` are real readings. `||` throws them away; `??` only steps in for `null` or `undefined`. `?.` never supplies a default at all.

blocks.promptMd: > `beaconName(signal)` returns the beacon name. Missing signal or missing beacon gives `"unknown"`, but an empty name stays empty. Print `beaconName({ beacon: { name: "north" } })`.

hintLadder.md: Reading `.beacon.name` on an empty object throws. You need the chain to stop instead.
`?.` returns undefined at the first missing link. `??` then fills in the fallback.
`const label = record?.inner?.label ?? "none"` reads two levels and defaults only when something was missing.

description: Reach through a record that may be missing without crashing. The question mark dot stops at the first gap, and it is not a default.
